cohort: The study included 22,393 full-term children born in Iceland from 2010 to 2019, categorized by their early life antibiotic exposure and birth mode.
finding: Children with early antibiotic exposure had significantly higher rates of infections and antibiotic use later in childhood, and a 2-fold increased risk of asthma diagnosis, compared to controls.
mod_finding: Children born by elective cesarean section also showed a significantly higher risk of infections and antibiotic use later in childhood compared to those born vaginally without antibiotic exposure.
